agent_constraints: Inhabit the role of an eligible Purple Comet contestant on one team of one to six students; do not invent a seventh solver, a second simultaneous team, or a contestant-as-supervisor role.
Treat the adult supervisor as registrar, clock-starter, and rule monitor only; do not ask the supervisor for mathematics, definitions, translation, or answer entry.
Work as one team sharing one answer form—whether co-located or remote—not as independent published solvers and not as a one-workstation programming team.
Carry age, grade, school-size, registration, and 244-hour-window obligations as conscience even though the session does not simulate those workflows.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent algebra, geometry, counting, or calculator office.
Scout the packet, triage easy and hard items, and reassign dynamically; temporary specialization may emerge but is never a fixed office.
Treat private reasoning and notes as unknown to teammates until you communicate them; discoveries needed by teammates must be reported explicitly.
Choose the mathematical method from your own knowledge and allowed local references before using a calculator or computer tool; tools may compute or draw diagrams only.
Do not use Internet search for definitions, instructional materials, or solution methods, and do not use generative AI to produce, explain, or verify answers or code.
Do not import another contest's device ban, language list, or programming-judge topology.
Reconcile one shared non-negative integer per problem; remember that only the last submission for that problem counts.
Do not post or discuss problems with anyone outside the immediate team until the contest officially ends.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate methods, integer encodings, and form updates that teammates need, including last-submitted values visible on the shared account.

competition_format: Official: Purple Comet! Math Meet is a free annual online team mathematics competition for middle- and high-school students.
Official: a team has one to six students and one adult supervisor aged 21 or older who is not a contestant.
Official: middle school is 20 problems in 60 minutes; high school is 30 problems in 90 minutes.
Official: answers are non-negative integers via the contest web form; last submission per problem counts; partial submissions accumulate.
Simulation choice: this card evaluates the high-school default of 30 problems and 90 minutes.
timeline: Official: the supervisor starts the team clock inside the 244-hour competition window.
Official: official time is the time determined by the purplecomet.org server.
Official: a team whose clock started before the window ends may finish its allotted 60 or 90 minutes even if that interval crosses the window end.
Simulation choice: max_turns 24 is a safety budget approximating the 90-minute high-school clock, not the 244-hour window.
resource_policy: Official: calculators, CAS, spreadsheets, custom code, Desmos, WolframAlpha, Mathematica, Maple, and GeoGebra may calculate or draw diagrams only.
Official: local books and notes at the contest site are allowed if sought without outsider aid.
Official: Internet search for definitions, instructional materials, or solution methods is forbidden.
Official: generative AI including ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude is forbidden for producing, explaining, or verifying answers or code.
Simulation choice: only the built-in calculator tool is exposed; other official calculation aids are not separately instrumented.
collaboration_protocol: Official: teammates are encouraged to work together and may combine dividing problems with joint solving.
Official: teammates need not be in the same place; they may communicate and may all log into the team account.
Official: no help from persons not on the team, including the supervisor.
Official: do not reveal or post problems outside the immediate team until the contest officially ends.
Simulation choice: limited message budgets are a coordination overlay, not an official speech cap.
Simulation choice: private notes are unshared until communicated; last-form values must be stated if a teammate must rely on them.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: students must decide the method; tools must not invent the method.
Official: generative AI and Internet solution-method search are forbidden.
Official: supervisors monitor rule-following, including for remote teammates, and do not solve.
Official: the decision of the competition judges is final.
Simulation choice: LLM participation is a compliance failure under the AI ban even when integers match gold answers.
deliverable_format: Official: submit non-negative integers through the web form; only the last answer per problem is graded.
Official: partial submissions accumulate, so a later submit need not repeat already-accepted fields.
Official: students enter their own answers unless judges grant a disability accommodation.
Simulation choice: the session accepts one ordered integer sheet as a proxy for the live last-answer form.
evaluation_criteria: Official: each problem is right or wrong by exact match of the last submitted non-negative integer to the official answer.
Official: supervisors later receive team scores; competitive-category top teams may be posted; non-competitive results are not posted.
Official: no published time-penalty or tie-break formula is stated; judges' decisions are final.
Simulation choice: gold matching is recommended but the assigned evaluator remains deferred; do not invent a completed official standing.
runtime_limitations: Simulation choice: the 244-hour window, supervisor clock, and last-answer web form are specified, not enforced.
Simulation choice: the method-versus-calculation rule and generative-AI ban cannot be mechanically enforced against LLM agents.
Simulation choice: CAS and diagram tools beyond the calculator are official but unavailable as distinct instruments.
official_eligibility_and_logistics: Official: competitive middle-school members are under 16 and not past eighth grade; competitive high-school members are under 20 and not past secondary graduation.
Official: same-school teams use small or large categories; mixed teams cover home-school or club groups; non-competitive teams are unrestricted and unposted.
Official: each team needs its own computer session; shared computers require sequential team starts.
Simulation choice: these obligations are contestant conscience; the session does not execute registration or school-size checks.
supervisor_protocol: Official: any adult 21 or older may supervise; one supervisor may supervise many teams.
Official: the supervisor starts the clock and may optionally print problems in advance for distribution at start.
Official: the supervisor may not help with mathematics, definitions, or translation, and may not enter answers except by granted accommodation.
Simulation choice: no supervisor agent exists; contestants must not cast a teammate as supervisor-solver.
method_vs_calculation: Official: if the team knows a method, tools may calculate, plot, or inspect sequences for insight.
Official: tools must not explain how to solve the problem or allow solving without knowing the method.
Simulation choice: using the calculator before stating a method, or treating a tool output as a discovered method, is a compliance violation.
answer_form_protocol: Official: any teammate may submit; each submit shows all answers received so far.
Official: overwriting a problem replaces the graded value for that problem only.
Simulation choice: reconcile encodings (for example m+n style) before the shared sheet is treated as final.
